paragraphs: It is argued that advertising has positive economic effects. However, some others say it has negative social effects because it could make people dissatisfied with who they are and what they have. Personally, I think there are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

Admittedly, one might argue that advertising brings undeniable economic benefits. This is predicted on the assumption that with the presence of positive economic effects from advertising, people will be supported by it can creative content, appealing visual effects.

Furthermore, spending power is increased, leading to production being encouraged and more employment opportunities, greater state revenues through taxation so that they can build a stronger economy. We can see in Vietnam that Shopee or Lazada in VN rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract customers, boosting not only their sales but also the entire digital retail sector. Through this, advertising creates jobs in marketing, media, and design; therefore it was very important driver of economic activity.

On this side of the debate, advertising also has negative social consequences. Any advertisements constantly show images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards or luxury possessions, which can make viewers dissatisfied with their own lives. Young people in particular may feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok and Facebook. This issue leads to frustration when they cannot afford them. Advertising promotes materialistic values and a money-driven culture in the long run.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that promoting advertising has both views about positive economic effects and negative social effects. Both views are valid to some extent; advertising can contribute to social dissatisfaction and play a crucial role in economic development.

On the one hand, supporters of advertising often point to the undeniable economic benefits it can bring. Creative content and appealing visual effects can stimulate consumer demand. Furthermore, spending power increases and production is encouraged, resulting in more employment opportunities and greater state revenues through taxation. This can build a stronger economy. In Vietnam, Shopee and Lazada rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract customers, boosting both their sales and the digital retail sector. Furthermore, advertising creates jobs in marketing, media, and design, making it an important driver of economic activity.

Those on the other side of the debate, however, argue that advertising entails negative social consequences. Advertisements constantly show images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards, and luxury possessions, which can make viewers dissatisfied with their own lives. Young people in particular may feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok and Facebook, leading to frustration when they cannot afford them. In the long run, advertising promotes materialistic values and a money-driven culture.
In conclusion, I believe both views are valid to a certain extent. Advertising can contribute to social dissatisfaction while playing a crucial role in economic development.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that the news media have too much influence on people's lives today and this is a negative problem. Personally, I am of the same school of thought but not all.

Admittedly, one might of argue that the news media have too much influence on people lives today. This is predicated initially on the assumption that in modern life today, the widespread access to smartphones and the Internet, these technologies allow people to follow the news instantly wherever and whenever they are, so checking news become a regular part of their routine. and the intense competition among news outlets lead to gain attention, most media agencies focus on breaking content and present it in a highly sensationalized manner with dramatic headline and eye-catching visuals, so that it make people reinforce the overall impact of news on public opinion.

However, I strongly believe that beside the negative influence on people lives today, the news media can having many good effects to our lives. The news media expose to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news and make overwhelmed people feel overly anxious, helpless and even in situations that do not directly affect them. However, the news coverage warn the public to existing and looming problems in society, crime, natural disasters, or political corruption. We can see the natural disaster about Yagi flood in Vietnam two years ago, the news media was always up the new information about it. Its movements [chưa đọc rõ] to people in the area location [chưa đọc rõ] on TV and save many people lives. paragraphs: There is an opinion that news reporting exerts an excessive influence on people's lives today and that this trend is harmful. Personally, I agree that this influence is considerable, although I do not consider it entirely negative.

Admittedly, the news media exert a considerable influence on people's lives today. Initially, in modern life, the widespread access to smartphones and the Internet allows people to use these technologies to follow the news instantly wherever and whenever they are; consequently, checking news becomes a regular part of their routine. Furthermore, the intense competition among news outlets encourages most media agencies to seek attention by focusing on breaking content and presenting it in a highly sensationalized manner with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals, thereby reinforcing the overall impact of news on public opinion.

However, I strongly believe that besides their negative influence on people's lives today, the news media can have many good effects on our lives. The news media expose people to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news and make them feel overwhelmed, overly anxious and helpless, even in situations that do not directly affect them. However, the news coverage warns the public to existing and looming problems in society, such as crime, natural disasters, or political corruption. We can see this in the natural disaster of the Yagi flood in Vietnam two years ago, when the news media were constantly providing new information about it. Updates about its movements were broadcast to people in the area on television, helping save many people's lives. This very instance clearly suggests how the news has many good effects on people's lives today. It helps individuals have better information and be more prepared to respond to potential threats, enabling them to handle risks in an increasingly complex society.

In conclusion, I am personally convinced that news media exert a considerable influence on people's lives today, although this is not an entirely negative development, as news reporting has many good effects on people's lives.

paragraphs: It is argued that some people think that school should reward students who show the best academic result, while others believe that it is more important to reward students who show improvements. Personally, I am from my perspective there are some case to be made for both sides of the argument.

Admittedly, one might argue that school should reward students who show the best academic result. This is predicated, initially, on the assumption that students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies will deserve their praises and privileges such as qualification of money or membership, this way encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards. So they can propel towards overall academic gains. This kind of competitive have seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded, they are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition so this lead to it may enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, I strongly believe that beside the students who rewarded for their best academic results, students who show improvements also need to have rewards. When only a few smart students can come first and received the rewards, it cause others to think that their effort is futile because they can't surpass those outstanding individuals. It make them so they prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened then lead to gradually lose the incentive to study. We can see almost competitions in the world always have many rewards for both groups such as The Face Viet Nam, Miss Universe, we need to emphasize improvements, then encourages all students to be diligently in their studies, help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constant desire to outdo themselves benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that school should reward students who show the best academic results and it's very important to also reward students who show improvements.

paragraphs: Some people favour rewarding students with the best academic results, while others place greater importance on recognising students who make progress. From my perspective, there are strong cases to be made for rewarding both high-achieving students and those who make progress.

Supporters of rewarding high achievers argue that schools should reward students who show the best academic results. This is predicated on the assumption that students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards. Their effort may contribute to stronger academic results overall. Furthermore, this kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Students may become used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which may enable them to achieve success in later life.

Advocates of rewarding progress argue that besides rewarding high-achieving students, schools should also reward those who show improvements. Initially, if only a few high-achieving students receive rewards, this can cause others to think that their effort is futile. This is because they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they may feel overwhelmed and disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. Furthermore, schools should recognise progress as well as top performance. This can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help them understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constant desire to outdo themselves may benefit them more than the determination to defeat others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that schools should reward students who show the best academic results and schools should also reward students who show improvements.
